title: Manna, hearing, Cornelius and Simon
english: From what is written — [[I have taken the Levites from the midst of the children of Israel in place of every firstborn who opens the womb >> Bible:Numbers 3:12]] — and the rest. Scripture says of the manna that whoever took it as God commanded was nourished by it; whoever took it against the divine measure did not enjoy it as living food, but [[worms swarmed out of it >> Bible:Exodus 16:20]]. So our manna is the word of God: the same sermon becomes salvation for some and punishment for others. How much better for some never to hear the word than to hear it with malice or hypocrisy — though truly better still is to hear with a good and simple heart, that it may [[bear fruit in good soil >> Bible:Luke 8:15]]. We say this in preface for catechumens — and for some of the baptized. [[Not all who are of Israel are Israel >> Bible:Romans 9:6]]; not all washed with water are at once washed with the Holy Spirit; and not every catechumen is a stranger to the Spirit. [[Cornelius >> Bible:Acts 10:44-47]] received the Spirit before the water; [[Simon >> Bible:Acts 8:13-21]] had baptism yet lost the gift by hypocrisy. Do not doubt that Corneliuses still stand among catechumens and Simons among the faithful. I say this to correct myself; I too am one of those who hear the word of God.
translator_notes: Copy-text Baehrens GCS 30 / Origenes Werke VII (1921), Rufinus Latin.
True OET: no ANF; do not copy Scheck FOTC (Numbers).
After Homilia I tip 2aeec79a; Hexateuch continuation.

title: Levites taken from the midst for the firstborns
english: But let us hear what the divine word says to Moses: [[Behold, I have taken the Levites from the midst of the children of Israel in place of every firstborn who opens the womb; they shall be mine — for every firstborn is mine >> Bible:Numbers 3:11-13]]. Levi is Leah’s third-born, yet those who are not firstborn by nature are taken into the firstborns’ place. With God the firstborns are not those who lead by bodily birth, but those whose open heart-purpose receives the grace of the firstborn portion. What is “from the midst”? The Shunammite answers, [[I dwell in the midst of my people >> Bible:2 Kings 4:13]]. And more magnificently John says of the Savior, [[There stands one in your midst whom you do not know >> Bible:John 1:26]]. Christ is said to stand in the middle; his imitator is said to dwell in the middle — for [[no one is clean from filth >> Bible:Job 14:4]]. Levites “from the midst” are those who have not known their own right and left, but follow the law of God. Better to be taken than merely to be born first. Stand fixed in the middle; do not lean into sin — and you will be taken from the midst into the number of the firstborns. So much for the word: [[I will take the Levites from the midst of the children of Israel >> Bible:Numbers 3:12]].

title: Camp order and the church of the firstborns
english: But if it seems good, let us return to the order of the history in Numbers and contemplate the mystery of the firstborns. The twelve tribes are set by threes toward the four quarters: [[Judah to the east with Issachar and Zebulun >> Bible:Numbers 2:3-9]]; Reuben to the west with Simeon and Gad; Ephraim to the south with Benjamin and Manasseh; Dan to the north with Naphtali and Asher. In the middle, nearest to God, the Levites are stationed around the tabernacle. The letter of the law sows sacramental seeds so that we may climb from earthly things to heavenly. Ascend, then, hearer, in mind above the heavens: seek there the tabernacle where [[Jesus our forerunner has entered >> Bible:Hebrews 6:20]] and [[now appears before the face of God, interceding for us >> Bible:Hebrews 7:25]]; seek there the camp-orders and the [[church of the firstborn enrolled in heaven >> Bible:Hebrews 12:23]]. Not all approach the same things: some come to Mount Zion; better ones to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem; others to the church of the firstborns.

title: Opening the womb and Christ the firstborn
english: And what it says — [[for every firstborn who opens the womb >> Bible:Numbers 3:12]] — is not easy to unfold. Not everyone who opens a womb is at once worthy of the firstborn sanctification; the psalm says [[sinners are estranged from the womb; they went astray from the belly; they spoke lies >> Bible:Psalm 58:3]] — which cannot stand by the bare letter. We must seek that womb which every firstborn sanctified to God opens. God once [[opened Leah’s womb >> Bible:Genesis 29:31]] and Rachel’s. [[They shall be mine as Levites; every firstborn is mine from the day I struck the firstborn of Egypt >> Bible:Numbers 3:12-13]]. Who struck Egypt’s firstborns — the principalities and powers? My Lord Jesus Christ, [[the firstborn of all creation >> Bible:Colossians 1:15]], who [[disarmed the rulers and authorities, triumphing over them on the cross >> Bible:Colossians 2:15]]. Unless he had struck them down, firstborn sanctification could never have reached us. He, [[firstborn from the dead >> Bible:Colossians 1:18]], takes us who believe into the order of the firstborns — if we hold the grace firm to the end.
